In particular smooth approximations with bounded H^gamma norm converge in C([0,T];L^2); M=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma) is bounded by 1+A(T,gamma,R).
propositions.origin: problem.md:105-122; sign and homogeneous/inhomogeneous norm bridge.

propositions.statement: For all I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and h=b-a<=1, all 0<=sigma<=1 and paths f_j in L^infty(I;H^sigma) with weak derivatives in L^infty(I;H^(-pstar)), Ctri satisfies ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_(X(I))+C*||f_i||_(L^infty H^(-pstar))*product_{j!=i}||f_j||_(L^infty L^2), each i=1,2,3. For time-independent inputs, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*h^sigma*product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma), including sigma=0. For 0<sigma<=1 choose a_sigma=1/2-sigma for sigma<1/2, a_sigma=1/8 for sigma=1/2, a_sigma=0 for sigma>1/2. Then 0<=a_sigma<1, and for every f in H^sigma and g in H^a_sigma, ||fg||_2<=C_sigma||f||_(H^sigma)||g||_(H^a_sigma). For any constant mean-zero w in H^sigma with ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M, 0<tau<=1 and a>=0, sup_[a,a+tau]||F_a(t;w)||_(H^a_sigma)<=C_(M,sigma)*tau^sigma and sup_[a,a+tau]||F_a(t;w)||_(H^(1+sigma))<=C_(M,sigma). All these are in the normalized norms, with constants uniform in endpoints and support.
propositions.origin: problem.md:334-369; explicit source normalization and stage-exponent specialization.

propositions.statement: For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, eta_tau(alpha,beta)=0 if alpha*beta=0; otherwise |eta_tau|<=2*min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau|<=tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|). For every nonzero integer quadruple a+b+c+d=0, N1<=3*N2 and, writing A=|ab|, B0=|cd|, one has (1/|d|)*min(A/B0,B0/A)<=3/Nthird(a,b,c,d), and |a+b|/max(A,B0)<=6/Nthird(a,b,c,d).
propositions.origin: problem.md:145-203; covariance and pointwise four-frequency majorants.

propositions.statement: There is an absolute C such that for all nonnegative x1,x2,x3,x4 in ell^2(Z\{0}), sum_{a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0} x1(a)x2(b)x3(c)x4(d)/Nthird(a,b,c,d)<=C*product_{j=1}^4||xj||_(ell^2). The sum is the supremum of finite positive partial sums; the same bound holds when it is restricted to any subset of quadruples.
propositions.origin: problem.md:204-251; dyadic summation with geometric smaller-scale gain.

propositions.statement: For 0<=sigma<=1, tau>0, any real base time a, and mean-zero fj in H^sigma, ||R2_(a,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||fj||_(H^sigma), uniformly in a,tau and Fourier support. The bound holds after inserting any multiplier of modulus <=1, including restriction to Phi=0 or Phi!=0. Polynomial approximation defines its unique continuous trilinear extension. Moreover, for 0<gamma<=1, mean-zero w in H^gamma with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, f in mean-zero L^2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1, ||R2_(a,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta). This estimate requires no H^gamma bound on f.
propositions.origin: problem.md:253-299; mixed remainder theorem including exponent zero and numerical-state corollary.

propositions.statement: There is an absolute C>0 such that the following bounds hold uniformly in time. For mean-zero f,g in L^2 and all real t, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(fg)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 whenever the latter is finite; ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2. For all A,A2 in H^1, the algebra bound is: ||A*A2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality/mean and is strongly continuous. For continuous, piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Also J_t is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). In particular F_a(t;f,g)=[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/6 for constant inputs. All bounded product maps extend from polynomials by density.
propositions.origin: problem.md:315-333,370-398; local Fourier product bounds and exact normal forms.

propositions.statement: For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau from Scheme is a continuous polynomial map from mean-zero L^2 to mean-zero L^2, preserving reality; Ftau maps L^2 continuously to H^1. Smooth data produce smooth iterates. For any trajectory produced by Scheme from smooth mean-zero data, f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n, the Interp construction has V(t_n)=f_n, V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1), is continuous and piecewise smooth in time and spatially smooth, and has mean-zero values, which are real whenever the initial datum is real. On each open step, V'=B_t(V,V)/2+mathcalR', where mathcalR'=-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. Thus mathcalR is continuous with the defining increments and the displayed residual identity holds a.e.
propositions.origin: problem.md:399-431,501-514,632-641; source scheme bridge and elementary well-definedness.

propositions.statement: Let 0<tau<=1, let u be a smooth real mean-zero exact KdV solution on [0,T], v=S_(-t)u, and M>=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma). On any step of the smooth twisted Scheme trajectory f_n, assume delta_n=||f_n-v(t_n)||_2<=1 and put q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. For Interp, with constants C_M depending only on M,gamma,T, uniformly in n,tau and support: sup_(I_n)||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_M, sup_(I_n)||F_n-F_(t_n)(t;v(t_n))||_(H^1)<=C_M*delta_n; sup_(I_n)(||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)+||F_n||_2)<=C_M*q_n; ||z_n||_(X(I_n))<=C_M; sup_(I_n)||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Dinv B_t(f_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M*q_n; sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_2<=C_M*q_n, ||Y_n||_(X(I_n))<=C_M*q_n and sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q_n. Here a_gamma=1/2-gamma if gamma<1/2, 1/8 if gamma=1/2, and 0 if gamma>1/2. No numerical H^gamma norm is used.
propositions.origin: problem.md:432-499; stage, endpoint correction, interpolation defect and weak smallness.

propositions.statement: For a smooth real mean-zero exact KdV solution u on [0,T], twist v=S_(-t)u, and smooth Scheme trajectory f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n, suppose M>=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma), 0<tau<=1, delta_n=||f_n-v(t_n)||_2<=1 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. Then Interp satisfies sup_(I_n)||rho_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and ||mathcalR'||_(L^infty(I_n;H^(-pstar)))<=C_M*q_n. On any I=[a,b] contained in [0,T] with a a grid point, h=b-a<=1, define e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2. If E_I<=1 then sup_I||mathcalR(t)-mathcalR(a)||_2<=C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))<=C_M. Intervals may end inside a step; derivative assertions hold a.e. All constants depend only on M,gamma,T and are uniform in n,tau and Fourier support.
propositions.origin: problem.md:501-540; stepwise residual calculation and accumulated interval estimates.

propositions.statement: For a smooth real mean-zero exact KdV solution u on [0,T], twisted path v=S_(-t)u, and the Interp path V of the smooth twisted Scheme trajectory, M>=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma), 0<tau<=1, every grid-start interval I=[a,b] of length h<=1 with E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2<=1 and every real N>=2 satisfy E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_M*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_M*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I, where e=v-V. The constant depends only on M,gamma,T, not a,b,N,tau,support, and the interval may end inside a step. Both normal-form endpoints are retained.
propositions.origin: problem.md:543-614; low/high decomposition with exact forcing normal form.

propositions.statement: There exist positive C and tau0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that for every smooth real mean-zero datum q with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, its exact solution and the unmodified Scheme satisfy sup_[0,T]||S_(-t)u(t)-V(t)||_2<=C*tau^gamma for Interp built from its twisted numerical trajectory. In particular max_(0<=n<=L)||u(t_n)-U^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. The constants are independent of higher Sobolev norms and spectral support.
propositions.origin: problem.md:615-631; restarted finite-block recurrence and continuity bootstrap.

propositions.statement: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the exact solution u and the fixed unfiltered scheme U defined below satisfy max_{0<=n<=L} ||u(n*tau)-U^n||_2 <= C*tau^gamma. The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation. Both constants are uniform over the entire initial-data ball, all such L, and Fourier support.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary q, with its properties introduced by the local antecedent L1.
Define (Jf)(x)=-f(-x) for every periodic distribution f.
Define Q=Jq.
Take the unique source flow of E001 with initial datum Q, at order gamma and horizon T, under L1.
For every integer n>=1 define p(n) by retaining the Fourier coefficients of Q at |k|<=n and setting all other coefficients to zero.
For every integer n>=1 set e(n)(x)=(exp(i*(n+1)*x)+exp(-i*(n+1)*x))/sqrt(2).
For every integer n>=1 set d(n)=sqrt(R^2-||p(n)||_(dot H^gamma)^2); nonnegativity of the radicand is proved in S002.
For every integer n>=1 set Qpad(n)=p(n)+(n+1)^(-gamma)*d(n)*e(n).
Choose K>=1 from E001(i), with sigma=gamma, b=T, B0=R and exact initial dot H^gamma norm R, as justified in S003. The choice depends only on T,gamma,R.
For every integer n>=1 take Upad(n) to be the unique source flow from datum Qpad(n), supplied by E001(ii)-(iii).
Set A=2^(gamma/2)*K, a positive constant depending only on T,gamma,R.
Set u(t)=J(U(t)), that is u(t,x)=-U(t,-x).
Set v(t)=S_(-t)u(t).
Set M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma). Its finiteness and bound are proved in S004.
Fix an arbitrary real B0; positivity and the comparison premise are assumed locally under L2.
Fix arbitrary qtilde with the properties assumed locally under L2.
Fix arbitrary Utilde, assumed under L2 to be the corresponding second solution constructed above.

locals.type: function of a positive real horizon and a positive real L2 bound
locals.declaration: For positive b and beta set C(b,beta)=C'(beta,0)*C_(beta,0)^b, using the constants supplied by E001(iv); enlarge to a positive constant if necessary.
Fix an arbitrary sequence qapp, with its approximation properties assumed locally under L3.
Under L3 take the smooth flows uapp(j) for qapp(j), obtained by applying E001 to the reflected smooth data and the transformation in S004.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary q and introduce L1: q is real and mean-zero, q belongs to H^gamma and ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R. H001-H003 give T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. Define Jf(x)=-f(-x) and Q=Jq. Its Fourier formula is hat(Jf)(k)=-hat f(-k); thus J is an involution preserving reality, mean zero and every H^s and mean-zero dot H^s norm, by reindexing the even weighted square sums. In particular ||Q||_2<=R and ||Q||_(dot H^gamma)<=R. Apply E001(i)-(iii) with sigma=gamma, b=T, B0=R and source datum Q (in (ii) one may take rho=gamma/2). This supplies a unique source solution U in C([0,T];dot H^gamma), satisfying its coefficientwise integral equation and conserving ||U(t)||_2=||Q||_2 for every t. D003 gives continuity also in H^gamma. The bound furnished at this point is allowed to depend on the exact norm ||Q||_(dot H^gamma); no uniformity over the ball is inferred here. If q is smooth, apply E001 at each higher order sigma>gamma. These source flows embed into the gamma class and uniqueness identifies them with U. Smooth periodic data have finite norms at every order by repeated integration by parts in the Fourier formula. Conversely the Cauchy-Schwarz estimate for differentiated Fourier series gives H^s into C^j when s>j+1/2. Hence these higher-order continuities and the source evolution yield spatial smoothness and then, by iterating that polynomial evolution, all mixed time and spatial derivatives.

produces.statement: Under L1, Q=Jq is real and mean-zero with ||Q||_2<=R and ||Q||_(dot H^gamma)<=R. The source flow U with datum Q exists uniquely, belongs to C([0,T];H^gamma), satisfies the source coefficientwise integral equation and conserves L2. Smooth q gives smooth U.

argument.text: Construct approximations whose exact homogeneous norm is fixed. For every integer n>=1 let p(n) be the Fourier truncation of Q to |k|<=n, and set e(n)(x)=(exp(i*(n+1)*x)+exp(-i*(n+1)*x))/sqrt(2). The Fourier supports of p(n) and e(n) are disjoint, e(n) is real and mean-zero, ||e(n)||_2=1 and ||e(n)||_(dot H^gamma)=(n+1)^gamma. Deleting nonnegative summands shows ||p(n)||_(dot H^gamma)<=R. Thus d(n)=sqrt(R^2-||p(n)||_(dot H^gamma)^2) is defined and lies in [0,R]. Define Qpad(n)=p(n)+(n+1)^(-gamma)*d(n)*e(n). Orthogonality of these disjoint Fourier supports gives ||Qpad(n)||_(dot H^gamma)^2=||p(n)||_(dot H^gamma)^2+d(n)^2=R^2, so its exact norm equals R. Each Qpad(n) is a smooth real mean-zero trigonometric polynomial, and ||Qpad(n)||_2<=||Qpad(n)||_(dot H^gamma)=R because all its frequencies are nonzero integers. Finally ||Qpad(n)-Q||_2<=||p(n)-Q||_2+R*(n+1)^(-gamma) tends to zero: the first term is a tail of the convergent Fourier norm series, and the second tends to zero since gamma>0. Only L2 convergence of these padded approximations is asserted.

produces.statement: For every integer n>=1, Qpad(n) is smooth, real and mean-zero, ||Qpad(n)||_(dot H^gamma)=R and ||Qpad(n)||_2<=R. Moreover Qpad(n) converges to Q in L2 as n tends to infinity.

argument.text: Apply E001(i) at sigma=gamma, b=T and B0=R to the data Qpad(n). Every one of these data has the same exact initial dot H^gamma norm R by F002. Consequently the dependence allowed in E001(i) is evaluated only at the fixed tuple (gamma,T,R,R): choose its finite bound, enlarged to K>=1, depending only on T,gamma,R. It bounds the Galerkin approximations for every Qpad(n), without any supremum over different exact initial norms. For each n, E001(ii) passes that same bound to a source integral solution, and E001(iii) identifies it with the unique continuous flow Upad(n). Thus ||Upad(n)(t)||_(dot H^gamma)<=K for almost every t. Continuity in dot H^gamma upgrades this to every t in [0,T]: a strict violation would persist on a nonempty relative time interval, contradicting the almost-everywhere bound. Now apply E001(iv) to Upad(n) and U with theta=0, b=T and B0=2*R. Their initial L2 norms sum to at most 2*R. The source twists preserve the L2 distance, so this gives sup_[0,T]||Upad(n)(t)-U(t)||_2<=C'(2*R,0)*C_(2*R,0)^T*||Qpad(n)-Q||_2, which tends to zero by F002. For each fixed t in [0,T] and integer m>=1, the finite sum sum_{0<|k|<=m}|k|^(2*gamma)*|hat U(t,k)|^2 is the limit of the corresponding sums for Upad(n)(t), since L2 convergence implies convergence of each Fourier coefficient. Each such sum is at most K^2. Taking the supremum over m, the definition of the nonnegative Fourier norm series yields ||U(t)||_(dot H^gamma)<=K. Since t was arbitrary, this is a bound on the entire time interval. This establishes uniformity on the original ball by approximation and stability, without a monotonicity or local boundedness assumption on E001's norm dependence.

produces.statement: There is a finite K>=1 depending only on T,gamma,R, chosen from E001 at exact initial homogeneous norm R and initial L2 bound R, such that sup_[0,T]||U(t)||_(dot H^gamma)<=K for the arbitrary datum q under L1.

argument.text: Set A=2^(gamma/2)*K and u(t,x)=-U(t,-x)=J(U(t)). At (t,-x), u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx. Therefore u_t+u_xxx=-U*U_x=u*u_x=partial_x(u^2)/2 and u(0)=q. For rough data these identities hold distributionally: products of L2 functions are L1 by Cauchy-Schwarz, and product differences obey ||fg-f1*g1||_1<=||f-f1||_2*||g||_2+||f1||_2*||g-g1||_2. Thus the continuous L2 source paths have continuous L1 squares and continuous bounded product Fourier coefficients. Its coefficientwise integral equations can be tested against smooth space-time functions, whose Fourier coefficients decay faster than the polynomial derivative factors; this gives the distributional equation. Reflection is involutive, so uniqueness transfers from the source. Conversely any solution in the stated continuous class transforms to the source coefficientwise integral class by testing each Fourier mode, so the same uniqueness applies. Norm preservation by J, F003 and D003 imply sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=2^(gamma/2)*K=A. It is continuous into H^gamma, and smooth if q is smooth by F001. Define v(t)=S_(-t)u(t). The multiplier in D004 has modulus one and conjugate values at opposite frequencies, so S_t preserves these norms, reality and mean zero. Strong continuity follows by checking finitely many coefficients and bounding the remaining weighted tail by four times the norm tail. Hence v is also continuous in H^gamma and has the same time-dependent norms as u. Differentiating each integrated Fourier equation with the multiplier exp(-i*t*k^3) cancels the linear term, giving v'=S_(-t)partial_x[(S_t v)^2]/2=B_t(v,v)/2 as a distributional identity. The expression defining B is valid here on L2 inputs: each product coefficient is bounded by the product of their L2 norms; after the derivative its magnitude is at most |k| times that product, so the H^(-2) squared norm is bounded by sum_k k^2*<k>^(-4) times the squared product of the input norms, a finite series. Thus the smooth formula extends continuously to these inputs and agrees distributionally. Finally set M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma); this is finite and at most 1+A.

produces.statement: Under L1, u is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional KdV solution with datum q, smooth when q is smooth. It satisfies sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A, with positive A=2^(gamma/2)*K depending only on T,gamma,R. The twist v=S_(-t)u has the same norms and satisfies v'=B_t(v,v)/2 distributionally; M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma)<=1+A.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary B0,qtilde,Utilde and assume locally L2: B0>0, qtilde is a second datum of the asserted real mean-zero H^gamma class, Utilde is its constructed solution, and ||q||_2+||qtilde||_2<=B0. The reflected paths Ju and JUtilde are the source flows with data Jq and Jqtilde, by the equation conversion and uniqueness above. Apply E001(iv) with theta=0 and b=T. Mean-zero dot H^0 equals L2, and both the source Fourier twist and J preserve the L2 distance. With C(T,B0)=C'(B0,0)*C_(B0,0)^T (enlarged if necessary), this gives sup_[0,T]||u-Utilde||_2<=C(T,B0)||q-qtilde||_2. Discharge L2 and quantify these comparison objects. For the approximation assertion, fix an arbitrary sequence qapp and assume locally L3: its terms are smooth, real and mean-zero, converge to q in L2, and have a common finite H^gamma bound. Apply E001 at each reflected smooth datum to get its smooth source flow, and set uapp(j) to be the reflected target flow; its existence follows at every positive Sobolev order. The common H^gamma bound gives a common L2 bound, so E001(iv), applied directly to each of these source flows and U, yields sup_[0,T]||uapp(j)-u||_2<=C(T,B0)||qapp(j)-q||_2 for one positive B0 bounding all the initial L2 norm sums. Therefore uapp converges to u in C([0,T];L2). Discharge L3 and quantify qapp. In particular choose qapp to be the symmetric Fourier truncations of q. They are smooth, real and mean-zero, have H^gamma norm at most R and converge to q in H^gamma (hence in L2), by the tail formula for the norm series. Thus u is precisely the smooth-approximation solution specified in D020; the comparison also makes its approximation limit independent of the chosen bounded sequence. All clauses for u,v,A,M are already established in F004, and A was chosen using only T,gamma,R. Discharge L1 and universally quantify q to obtain N001 in full.

applications.bindings: Use (i)-(iii) with sigma=gamma, b=T, source datum Q=Jq=-q(-x), B0=R and, in (ii), rho=gamma/2. Only a possibly exact-norm-dependent bound is claimed here.
hypothesis_checks: L1 and the Fourier formula for J give real mean-zero source data on the normalized torus; H001 gives T>0.
H002 gives gamma>0 and 0<gamma/2<gamma. L1 and D003 give finite homogeneous norm.
The initial L2 norm is at most R by L1 and norm preservation. Clause (iv) is not used in this application.

applications.bindings: For smooth q, apply (i)-(iii) at every sigma>gamma with b=T, source datum Q=Jq and B0=R; uniqueness at gamma identifies the resulting flows.
hypothesis_checks: Under L1 and the smooth-data conditional, Q is smooth, real and mean-zero; T>0 by H001.
Smoothness gives finite norms at every chosen sigma>gamma>0; for (ii) choose any rho between zero and sigma.
The reflected initial L2 norm is at most R. Clause (iv) is not used here.

applications.bindings: Apply (i)-(iii) for every Qpad(n), with sigma=gamma, b=T, B0=R and exact initial dot H^gamma norm equal to R; choose rho=gamma/2 in (ii). K is the common bound at this one fixed tuple of numerical arguments.
hypothesis_checks: F002 proves every Qpad(n) is real and mean-zero on the torus; H001 supplies T>0.
H002 supplies the permitted orders. F002 proves the exact finite homogeneous norm R for every datum, rather than merely an upper bound by R.
F002 gives ||Qpad(n)||_2<=R. The bound of (i) passes through (ii) to the unique flow of (iii); clause (iv) is not part of this application.

applications.bindings: Use (iv) with theta=0, b=T, B0=2*R and source flows Upad(n),U for every integer n>=1.
hypothesis_checks: F001 and F002 give the real mean-zero source data and the source flows supplied by (ii)-(iii); H001 gives the positive horizon.
theta=0 is in (-1,0], and both flows have positive order gamma and hence belong to the L2 class.
F001 gives ||Q||_2<=R and F002 gives ||Qpad(n)||_2<=R, so their initial norm sum is <=2*R. H003 gives 2*R>0.

applications.bindings: Use (iv) with theta=0, b=T, bound B0 and source flows Ju,JUtilde, with respective data Jq,Jqtilde, under the temporary antecedent L2.
hypothesis_checks: L1,L2 and the established construction give real mean-zero source data and flows; H001 gives T>0.
Both flows are at positive order gamma; theta=0 is the permitted endpoint and dot H^0 equals L2 for mean-zero data.
L2 assumes the initial L2 norm sum is at most the positive B0, and J preserves it.

applications.bindings: Under L3, apply (i)-(iii) at each smooth reflected datum J(qapp(j)), b=T, at order gamma and every higher positive order, using any positive common upper bound for their initial L2 norms. No common higher-order a priori bound is inferred in this application.
hypothesis_checks: L3 supplies smooth real mean-zero data and reflection preserves these properties; H001 supplies T>0.
Each smooth datum has finite homogeneous norms at every order used; gamma>0 and each chosen higher order is positive.
L3's bounded H^gamma norms bound the initial L2 norms. The common L2 upper bound is only an applicability parameter; exact higher norms may vary here.

applications.bindings: Under L3, apply (iv) to the source flows Juapp(j) and U with theta=0, b=T, and one positive B0 bounding ||qapp(j)||_2+||q||_2 for all j.
hypothesis_checks: L3 and the source construction give real mean-zero source flows and data; T>0 by H001.
All these flows are in the positive-order class, so the L2 endpoint theta=0 in (-1,0] is applicable.
The bounded H^gamma norms in L3 and L1 give a common finite upper bound for the required L2 norm sums; choose B0 larger than that bound. Reflection preserves all these norms.

Fix tau as described in the proof; hypotheses are introduced locally, not granted by its type.
Fix a as described in the proof; hypotheses are introduced locally, not granted by its type.

Consequently sup(||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)+||F_n||_2)<=C_M*q. Also z_n'=B_t(f,f)/2 and N006 imply ||z_n||_X<=C_M.

produces.statement: Under L1, q<=2, sup||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_M, sup||F_n-F_(t_n)(t;w,w)||_(H^1)<=C_M*delta, sup(||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)+||F_n||_2)<=C_M*q and ||z_n||_X<=C_M.

argument.text: Write A=F_(t_n)(t;w,w), D=F_n-A. For the exact-data square, N002's product estimate with f=partial_x(S_t A), g=S_t A gives ||partial_x[(S_t A)^2]||_2<=2*C_gamma||A||_(H^(1+gamma))||A||_(H^a_gamma)<=C_M*tau^gamma. For the difference of squares, (S_t F_n)^2-(S_t A)^2=(S_t D)*S_t(F_n+A). The H^1 algebra inequality of N006, F001, and ||D||_(H^1)<=C_M*delta bound its derivative by C_M*delta. Thus sup||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q. Integration gives sup||Q_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q. N005 applied to f and w gives ||R2^n_tau(f,f,f)||_2<=C_M*tau*q, hence ||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q.

produces.statement: Under L1 sup||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q and sup||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q.

argument.text: The exact formula Dinv B_t(f,F_n)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t F_n)] splits into the w product and the (f-w) product. By N002 and F001 the first is <=C_gamma||w||_(H^gamma)||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)<=C_M*q. The second is <=||f-w||_2||S_t F_n||_infinity<=C_M*delta by N006 and the uniform H^1 stage bound. Therefore sup||Dinv B_t(f,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q. Now Y_n'=B_t(f,F_n)+B_t(F_n,F_n)/2-W_n/tau. F002, boundedness of Dinv on mean-zero L^2, and integration from Y_n(t_n)=0 yield sup||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M*q and sup||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup||Dinv B_t(f,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q, sup||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q and sup||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M*q.

argument.text: For the strong Y_n bound apply N006's normal form to C_n(t)=integral B_s(f,F_n(s))ds, using F_n(t_n)=0 and F_n'=B_s(f,f)/2. Symmetry of J and its cubic identity give exactly C_n(t)=J_t(f,F_n(t))/3-C_[t_n,t](f,f,f)/6. The first term is O_M(q) in L^2 by N006 and F001. For the second use N002's constant-input estimate at exponent gamma on (w,w,w); expand its difference from (f,f,f) by trilinearity and use N002 at exponent zero, with ||f-w||_2=delta and ||f||_2+||w||_2<=2M. The result is C_M*(tau^gamma+delta)=C_M*q. Combining with Y_n=C_n+Q_n-((t-t_n)/tau)W_n and F002 proves sup||Y_n||_2<=C_M*q.

produces.statement: Under L1 sup||Y_n||_2<=C_M*q, with the exact normal form C_n(t)=J_t(f,F_n(t))/3-C_[t_n,t](f,f,f)/6.

argument.text: Because pstar>1, N006's mean-zero weak-norm comparison and F003 give sup||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q and sup||Y_n'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*q. Together with F004 these give ||Y_n||_X<=C_M*q. All constants depended only on the displayed low norms, gamma and the fixed horizon; no higher norm of f was used. Discharge L1 and quantify the data and step, yielding the asserted conclusion.

argument.text: Assume L1: the step hypotheses of N008 hold, with q=tau^gamma+delta_n<=2. In rho_n's first integral apply N006's normal form to B(Y_n,z_n). The boundary J(Y_n,z_n) is O_M(tau*q) by N008's Dinv Y_n bound and N006's asymmetric J bound. The integral J(Y_n',z_n) is also O_M(tau*q) by the Dinv Y_n' bound and ||z_n||_2<=C_M. Since z_n'=B_t(f_n,f_n)/2, the remaining integral is C(f_n,f_n,Y_n)/2 by N006. Apply N002's variable-path estimate with the negative slot on Y_n: its X norm is O_M(q), its negative norm is O_M(tau*q), and the constant f_n paths have bounded X and L^2 norms. Thus this integral is O_M(tau*q), for every partial step as well.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(I_n)||integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds||_2<=C_M*tau*q.

argument.text: For the second integral in rho_n apply the same normal form with Y_n in both slots. Its boundary is bounded by ||Dinv Y_n||_2||Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q^2; its derivative integral is bounded by tau*||Dinv Y_n'||_2||Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q^2. Since q<=2, these are O_M(tau*q). The endpoint correction is bounded by N008's ||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q. Thus sup||rho_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q. N007 gives mathcalR'=-B(Y_n,z_n)-B(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. N006's negative-norm product bound and N008 give ||mathcalR'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*(q+q^2+q)<=C_M*q. Discharge L1, retaining the fully quantified step estimates.

produces.statement: For every smooth exact path u with v=S_(-t)u and smooth mean-zero Scheme trajectory, if 0<tau<=1 and M>=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma), then every step index j0 with d0=||f_(j0)-v(t_(j0))||_2<=1 satisfies sup_(I_(j0))||rho_(j0)||_2<=C_M*tau*(tau^gamma+d0) and ||mathcalR'||_(L^infty(I_(j0);H^(-pstar)))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+d0).

argument.text: Now fix I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, and assume L2: e=v-V has E_I<=1, with the smooth paths and M bound as stated in the asserted conclusion. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps, and at every such step start delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. Summing F002's completed increments plus its valid partial-step bound gives sup||mathcalR(t)-mathcalR(a)||_2<=C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). Also v'=B_t(v,v)/2, so N006 bounds ||v||_X by C_M. From e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-mathcalR', ||e||_2<=E_I, ||v||_2<=M and the derivative part of F002 we obtain ||e'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I). Hence ||e||_X<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I), and V=v-e gives ||V||_X<=C_M. Discharge L2 and quantify. The a.e. step derivatives and continuous concatenations give exactly the asserted conclusion on arbitrary such intervals.

argument.text: Fix the smooth paths and I=[a,b], threshold N, step tau and size M, and assume L1: I starts at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, M>=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma), 0<tau<=1, E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, N>=2. Put g=v-e/2 and Fint(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,g)ds. N007 and the exact equation give e(t)=e(a)+Fint(t)-(mathcalR(t)-mathcalR(a)). For low frequencies, N006 gives ||Dinv P[(S_s e)(S_s g)]||_2<=C||e||_2||g||_2. Applying two spatial derivatives on |k|<=N bounds ||P_(<=N)B_s(e,g)||_2 by C_M*N^2*E_I, since S_s is unitary and ||g||_2<=M+1. Integration gives sup||P_(<=N)Fint||_2<=C_M*N^2*h*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, e(t)=e(a)+Fint(t)-(mathcalR(t)-mathcalR(a)) for t in I, and sup_(t in I)||P_(<=N)Fint(t)||_2<=C_M*N^2*h*E_I.

argument.text: Use N006's normal form, retaining both endpoints, together with e'=B(e,g)-mathcalR' and g'=B(v,v)/2-B(e,g)/2+mathcalR'/2. In the differentiated J terms, symmetry gives C(e,g,g)-C(e,g,e)/2=C(e,g,V), because g-e/2=V. The other cubic term is C(v,v,e)/2. The forcing terms combine as -J(mathcalR',g)+J(e,mathcalR')/2=-J(mathcalR',V). Therefore exactly Fint(t)=[J_s(e,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/3-C_[a,t](e,g,V)/3-C_[a,t](v,v,e)/6+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(mathcalR',V)ds. This identity holds across all pieces because the intermediate endpoints cancel. N006's H^1 J bound implies each endpoint after P_(>N) has norm <=C_M*N^(-1)*E_I; the initial endpoint is included even when e(a)!=0.

produces.statement: Under L1, for every t in I, Fint(t)=[J_s(e,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/3-C_[a,t](e,g,V)/3-C_[a,t](v,v,e)/6+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(mathcalR',V)ds. The L^2 norm of the projection P_(>N) of its two endpoint terms is <=C_M*N^(-1)*E_I.

argument.text: For any three qualifying paths f1,f2,f3, put Lcut=P_(<=N/3), Hcut=identity-Lcut. The trilinear telescoping expansion is C(f1,f2,f3)-C(Lcut f1,Lcut f2,Lcut f3)=C(Hcut f1,f2,f3)+C(Lcut f1,Hcut f2,f3)+C(Lcut f1,Lcut f2,Hcut f3). The all-low product has no output above N. Projections contract both parts of X, while ||Hcut fj||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||fj||_2. In each expanded term apply N002 with the negative norm on its specified high input. Hence ||P_(>N)C_[a,t](f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C*h*product||fj||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product||fj||_(L^infty L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e). N009 yields ||e||_X<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I) and bounds the other X norms by C_M; the product of L^2 norms contains E_I. Their total is therefore <=C_M*h*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, for all t in I the sum of the L^2 norms of P_(>N)C_[a,t](e,g,V)/3 and P_(>N)C_[a,t](v,v,e)/6 is <=C_M*h*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

argument.text: For the forcing term, on each intersected step use the actual residual formula N007: integral J(mathcalR',V)=-C(Y_n,z_n,V)-C(Y_n,Y_n,V)/2-tau^(-1)integral J(W_n,V). The intervals here are the completed or partial intersection with the step. The first two are O_M(tau*q_n) by N002, putting its negative norm on Y_n, using N008's ||Y_n||_X<=C_M*q_n and ||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C_M, and N009's bounded V norm on the intersection. H002 and 0<tau<=1 give tau^gamma<=1; since delta_n<=E_I<=1, q_n<=2 and q_n^2<=2*q_n. The last term is O_M(tau*q_n) by N008's ||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and the L^2 J bound from N006, since the intersection length is <=tau. Every intersected step starts in I, so delta_n<=E_I. There are at most h/tau+1 such steps. Summing bounds the entire forcing term, also after P_(>N), by C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(t in I)||P_(>N)integral_a^t J_s(mathcalR',V)ds||_2<=C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

argument.text: Combining F002-F004 gives sup||P_(>N)Fint||_2<=C_M*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. Use F001's low estimate and exact error identity, and N009's accumulated residual estimate, then take the time supremum. This gives E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_M*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_M*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. All estimates were uniform for partial final steps. Discharge L1 and quantify, obtaining the asserted conclusion.

Let K0>=1 dominate the constant C_M in N010 for the uniform M.
Set N=max(2,ceil(8*K0)); since pstar>1, K0*(N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))<=1/4.
Set Bcount=ceil(2*T/delta)+1.
Set K=max(1,3*K0*delta*(2^Bcount-1)).

For the datum under L3, choose its unique smooth exact solution from N001.

Construct V by Interp from the smooth twisted Scheme trajectory, whose continuity is supplied by N007.

Under L2 let tstar be the asserted first time with error norm one. If any crossing exists, continuity from e(0)=0 supplies such a time.

argument.text: H001-H003 fix T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. By N001 choose the common exact-solution bound M=1+A(T,gamma,R); it is independent of the datum in the ball. Let K0>=1 dominate the constant in N010 for this M. Fix arbitrary smooth q and integer L, and assume L3: q is real and mean-zero with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R, and L>0. Then N007 gives a global smooth finite-step trajectory and continuous interpolation. N001 gives the smooth exact solution, so e=v-V is continuous, starts at zero, and exists on the full interval. The constants M,K0 are chosen before q and L and involve no higher Sobolev norm. In what follows the only temporary restriction on error size is the bootstrap used to invoke N010.

produces.statement: There are common constants M,K0 depending only on T,gamma,R, and every smooth-data finite-step exact/interpolation error e is continuous with e(0)=0.

argument.text: Choose an integer N>=2 so large that K0*(N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))<=1/4; this is possible because pstar>0. Choose delta=min(1,1/[4*K0*(N^2+3)])>0 and restrict tau<=min(1,delta/2). On any grid-start interval with length h<=delta and E_I<=1, the small-frequency and timestep terms obey K0*(N^2*h+h+tau)<=K0*delta*(N^2+3)<=1/4. N010 therefore absorbs at most half of E_I and yields E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+3*K0*delta*tau^gamma. This estimate includes both endpoints and does not require e(a)=0.

produces.statement: For tau<=min(1,delta/2), every grid-start interval of length <=delta with E_I<=1 satisfies E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+3*K0*delta*tau^gamma.

argument.text: Split the grid into successive blocks of floor(delta/tau) steps, with a possibly shorter last block. The full block lengths lie in [delta/2,delta], so there are at most Bcount=ceil(2*T/delta)+1 blocks, independent of tau. Assuming L1: the bootstrap E<=1 holds on a prefix ending at any time, apply F002 block by block, using a partial final interval if that time is interior to a step. Induction starting at zero gives ||e|| on the first j blocks <=3*K0*delta*(2^j-1)*tau^gamma. Thus on every such prefix sup||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma, where choose K=max(1,3*K0*delta*(2^Bcount-1)). Discharge L1 to retain this conditional bound for every bootstrap-valid prefix.

produces.statement: For any prefix with error supremum <=1, sup||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma, where K depends only on T,gamma,R and tau<=min(1,delta/2).

argument.text: Set tau0=min(1,delta/2,(1/(4*K))^(1/gamma))>0. Assume L4: tau<=tau0. If L2: the error first reached norm one at some time tstar, continuity and e(0)=0 give an error supremum <=1 on [0,tstar]. F003, including its partial-last-block case, then gives ||e(tstar)||_2<=K*tau^gamma<=1/4, a contradiction. Discharge L2; continuity excludes all crossings and yields sup_[0,T]||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma. At grid points N007 gives V(t_n)=S_(-t_n)U^n and N006 gives unitarity, so the grid error equals ||u(t_n)-U^n||_2. Rename K as C, quantify the smooth datum and all L with tau<=tau0, and retain the constants chosen before them. Discharge L4 and L3; this proves the smooth-data estimate, uniformly in spectral support and higher norms.

Let U be the Scheme trajectory from u0 at step tau.

Choose the constant in N001's two-flow comparison at initial norm sum bound 2*R.

argument.text: H001-H003 give the fixed admissible T,gamma,R. Choose common C,tau0>0 from N011, depending only on these three. Fix arbitrary u0,L and assume L1: u0 is real mean-zero in H^gamma, ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, L is a positive integer and tau=T/L<=tau0. Set u0m=P_(<=m)u0. Fourier truncation preserves reality and zero mean, gives ||u0m||_(H^gamma)<=R, and the tail of the convergent weighted square sum shows u0m->u0 in H^gamma and L^2. N001 supplies the exact rough solution u and smooth solutions um with a common H^gamma bound. Its two-flow estimate at B0=2R gives sup_[0,T]||um-u||_2<=Kflow||u0m-u0||_2->0.

produces.statement: Under L1 smooth initial truncations stay in the same H^gamma ball and um converges to the prescribed exact solution u in C([0,T];L^2).

argument.text: Hold the currently chosen tau>0 and L finite. N007 proves continuity of Psi_tau on mean-zero L^2 directly for the exact unmodified formulas: inverse derivatives enter every nonlinear factor, H^1 products are bounded, P0(f^2) is continuous, and the finite coefficient tau^(-1) causes no problem at fixed tau. Therefore induction on n=0,...,L yields U_m^n->U^n in L^2. The base is u0m->u0; the step follows by applying the continuous Psi_tau. All these iterates are real and mean-zero by N007. This finite-step limit requires no uniform-in-tau stability of the map or numerical Sobolev bound.

produces.statement: Under L1, for the fixed tau and finite L, max_(0<=n<=L)||U_m^n-U^n||_2 tends to zero.

argument.text: N011 gives max_(0<=n<=L)||um(t_n)-U_m^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma with the same C,tau0 for every m. By F001-F002 each error vector converges in L^2; taking the maximum over the finite L+1 grid points and passing to the limit preserves the inequality. N006's unitary S_t and N007's grid matching justify exactly the same grid error used in the twisted smooth argument; no cutoff is introduced in Psi_tau. The limit u has the precise solution convention and distributional equation from N001, on the stated normalized torus. Discharge L1 and quantify u0 and L while retaining C,tau0 chosen first. This proves the target, including the full initial-ball uniformity, gamma=1 endpoint, and independence of Fourier support.
